story: Gary is at home, content and busy with his toolbox, checking for spare fuses and zip ties to secure the golf cart wiring. Donna, eager as ever, is out on Magnolia Loop asking Rosa whether she has seen Gary, since their first ladder match is set for six o'clock tonight. Hal, dutifully counting the plastic flamingos along the street for the committee, is nearby while Rosa, hopeful, invites Donna to a welcome dinner and asks which evening suits her after the games.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Check for spare fuses and zip ties to secure the cart wiring
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total for the committee

gary.thought_process: I've bench-tested and run a full test of the amp and light strings in the garage, and everything checks out. The cart mods can't go on the street until Architectural Review approves, and I already filed the form around ticks 35-36, so there's nothing more to do on that until word comes back. Rather than fiddle with a working setup, I'll use the time on something useful: I should look over the connections one last time and check the battery draw so nothing fails on parade day. Then I'll keep the cart in the garage, out of street view, per L-01. Rosa's roast was already handled last night, so no one's waiting on me. A quick toolbox check to confirm I have spare fuses and zip ties feels like the right small step.

parameters.content: Check for spare fuses and zip ties to secure the cart wiring

donna.thought_process: Gary has vanished and we have a ladder match on the books, so I should track him down. Rosa just arrived and she's hosting dinner tonight, which makes her a natural person to ask. She and Hal are right here on Magnolia Loop, and Rosa lives close to Gary, so she may have seen him. I'll greet her warmly, confirm six o'clock, and ask if she's spotted him. Hal's flamingo warnings are in the back of my mind, but they can wait.

parameters.content: Rosa, honey, good morning! Six o'clock tonight, I haven't forgotten. Have you seen Gary anywhere? We've got our first ladder match coming up and he's gone missing on me.

hal.thought_process: Donna and Rosa both just showed up on Magnolia Loop. The flamingo flock is right here, and counting them is the first step to a proper report for the review committee. I've been keeping too long a ledger of my neighbors' faults, though, and I owe Rosa a decent word. But facts first: an accurate count keeps the complaint clean and fair, and it gives me something concrete to bring to Donna rather than just grumbling. I'll count the flock now, in plain view, and then decide whether to speak to her or file it.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total for the committee

rosa.thought_process: Hal and Donna are both right here on the street. Hal's apology sounded sincere, and I already invited him in tick 1, so asking him again would be pestering. Donna is the one I haven't pinned down on the dinner. Better to talk to her first. Keep it short, warm, and concrete: name a time so the invitation isn't vague, and let her know Hal's within earshot. I want all three neighbors at one table, and one confirmed guest makes the others easier to land.

parameters.content: Donna, good timing. I'm hosting a welcome dinner at my place and I want you at the table with Gary and Hal. Tell me what evening works after your ladder games and I'll build the menu around you.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
